title: Phosphoric acid prices in cathode negotiations amid sulphur woes
gist: Chinese Tier 1 battery producers have begun writing purified phosphoric acid (PPA) into cathode active material price formulae because a sulphur supply shock — traced to the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on Russian gas processing plants — has sent PPA prices soaring. The squeeze has inverted the historical price relationship, pushing wet-process PPA above thermal-process PPA. insights.claim: Some Chinese Tier 1 battery producers have started including purified phosphoric acid (PPA) as an explicit input in their cathode active material (CAM) price negotiation formulae, a structural change in how LFP-chain contracts pass through raw material costs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Cost pass-through mechanics are migrating beyond lithium: watch CAM contract structures for PPA-indexed clauses, which shift input-price risk from cathode makers back onto cell buyers.

themes.theme: Sulphur shock from Hormuz and Russian strikes

insights.claim: Elevated purified phosphoric acid prices are attributed to global tightness in sulphur supply caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on Russian gas processing plants.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Two geopolitical events are transmitting directly into battery cathode costs via sulphur — an under-watched conflict-to-battery-cost channel that bypasses lithium entirely.
insights.quote: These elevated prices are a result of global tightness in sulphur supply, caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and drone attacks on Russian gas processing plants.

insights.claim: Sulphur, a by-product of oil and gas processing, is the chokepoint linking Middle East shipping disruption and strikes on Russian gas infrastructure to battery material costs, making energy-sector disruptions a leading indicator for phosphate cathode inputs.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Use sulphur availability as a transmission channel: hydrocarbon supply shocks now feed through to EV battery bills of material, not just to fuel prices.

insights.claim: The sulphur disruption has particularly hit wet-process purified phosphoric acid producers, which have cut output and delayed the commissioning of new projects.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Delayed wet-process commissioning means the PPA deficit is not a spot squeeze that resolves quickly — supply response is pushed out by project timelines.

insights.claim: In recent months wet-process purified phosphoric acid prices have climbed above thermal-process PPA prices, inverting a historical relationship in which thermal-process material commanded the premium because it requires significantly more electricity and higher-grade ore feedstock.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: A cost-curve inversion this stark signals genuine physical scarcity in wet-process routes and can make otherwise uneconomic thermal-process capacity the marginal supplier — watch for restarts of idled thermal capacity.
